disclaimer: These attestation-result objects are author-designed corpus fixtures appraised structurally by state_adapter.py. No cryptographic verification is performed, no TPM and no Veraison are involved, and nothing here is remote attestation. Expected labels are author-written, not external ground truth; adapter agreement with them measures the specification, not the world. Counts over these fixtures are corpus-design coverage, not rates.
decision_time_note: Fixed constant shared with policy-version-evidence-replay/corpus.json; timestamps compare lexicographically in fixed-width UTC Z form; both window boundaries are inclusive.
appraisal_order: 1 status contraindicated (or any non-affirming value, fail-closed) -> CONTRAINDICATED / state.contraindicated
3 observed_digest != reference_digest (or missing reference, fail-closed) -> REFERENCE_MISMATCH / state.reference
reference_digest_note: Digests are sha256 of the fixed strings 'runtime-measurement:v1' (reference) and 'runtime-measurement:tampered' (mismatch); they identify corpus constants, not any real runtime.

affirming-fresh-match.note: All gates pass; decision_time strictly inside the window.

contraindicated.note: Status gate fires although window and digest would both pass.

stale-match.note: Matching digest but expired 15 minutes before decision_time — the matching-but-stale case the former binary literal could not express.

fresh-mismatch.note: Fresh window but observed digest differs from reference — the fresh-but-mismatched case the former binary literal could not express.

stale-mismatch.note: Precedence fixture: rule 2 (stale) fires before rule 3 (mismatch).

boundary-fresh.note: decision_time == issued_at exactly; the lower window boundary is inclusive.

boundary-expiry.note: decision_time == expires_at exactly; the upper window boundary is inclusive.

contraindicated-stale-mismatch.note: Triple-fault precedence fixture: rule 1 wins over rules 2 and 3.
